Nema vs Lindy

Choose a channel coworker or a configurable automation agent.

Lindy lets teams build agents and multi-step workflows across business apps. Nema begins with a coworker inside each Slack channel.

The short answer

Lindy is a configurable agent and workflow platform. Teams can build agents with triggers, actions, conditions, knowledge, and connected applications. Lindy also offers templates for Slack bots and wider operational jobs. Nema starts in a different place. Each Slack channel gets a coworker that learns the channel's instructions, remembers its work, and keeps requests and approvals in the shared conversation.

Choose Nema when the channel itself should be the main interface and context boundary. Choose Lindy when an operator wants to design a reusable automation that spans apps, communication channels, and structured workflow steps.

A weekly operations report

An operations lead wants a report every Monday from an approved export, a project tracker, and the previous week's Slack decisions. The output should identify overdue items, conflicting statuses, and next actions. One update to the tracker should require review.

With Nema, the lead teaches the operations channel which files are authoritative, what counts as overdue, and who approves changes. Nema prepares the report in the channel thread. Teammates can add missing context before the lead approves the proposed tracker update. The correction remains useful to that channel's coworker on the next run.

With Lindy, an operator can build a recurring agent flow that starts on a schedule, reads selected sources, applies instructions, sends the report to Slack, and performs configured actions. Lindy is attractive when the process should run through a defined sequence and extend to email, meetings, or other destinations. Its visual and natural-language builder gives the automation owner explicit control over each step.

Choose Nema when

Choose Nema when team participation is part of the workflow. A request can begin as a normal Slack message, and the thread becomes the place where sources, corrections, and approvals accumulate. Separate channels can have separate coworkers instead of sharing one broad automation configuration.

Nema also fits teams that want requester-scoped app access and model choice. Test the exact connection because both access and available actions vary by application.

Choose Lindy when

Choose Lindy when a dedicated operator wants to build structured agents that run across apps and channels. Lindy publishes many templates for sales, support, scheduling, meetings, and communications. Its platform is a better conceptual fit when triggers, branching, and automation design are the main job.

Lindy can create a Slack bot that watches selected channels and responds based on instructions. Both products support Slack bots, scheduled agents, and connected actions. The choice is how the team wants to configure and supervise them.

Test the same exception

Give both products the same incomplete report. Remove an owner, use conflicting dates, and include one action that should not happen without approval. Observe how the agent exposes missing data, where a teammate corrects it, and whose credentials perform the external action.

Also measure setup and maintenance. Record who can change instructions, how a failed run is repaired, where logs appear, and how the team resumes work. A quick demo with clean inputs will not reveal these operating costs.

Common questions

Can Lindy work in Slack channels?

Yes. Lindy documents Slack bot templates, selected channel access, triggers, and Slack actions. Test direct messages, threads, mentions, and ambient triggers because their behavior can differ.

Does Nema replace Lindy workflows?

It can cover some conversational and recurring jobs, but Lindy is a broader workflow builder. Nema is designed for a shared coworker relationship in Slack rather than for visual automation design.

Which is easier for a nontechnical team?

That depends on the job. Nema starts with a channel conversation and explicit guidance. Lindy offers templates and natural-language building but still asks an owner to configure a workflow. Try the same report with the people who will maintain it.
